topic: This is a direct follow-up to the accepted experiment in the reuse directory listed above (see especially build_prompts.py, artifacts/prompts.jsonl with 600 prompts / 549 usable, and probe_train.py there). That run showed, for EleutherAI/pythia-1.4b under greedy decoding, that a single hidden state at the last prompt token predicts a sentence embedding of the full continuation with test cosine 0.4283 at layer 20 (vs mean baseline 0.2310, random 0.0616), retrieval Recall@5 0.759 vs chance 0.060, and that causal steering along the learned direction beat a random-direction control. Reuse that same prompt set (or a superset of it) so results are directly comparable across this run rather than starting from a different sample. NOTE: the shared server currently has only about 30GB of free disk -- be conservative about how many large model checkpoints you keep cached simultaneously, and prefer deleting a model checkpoint after you are done extracting what you need from it if disk gets tight. Now extend that work to address three priorities the user has specifically asked for, in whatever order and depth is achievable within the time budget -- design the concrete protocol for each yourself: (1) MOST IMPORTANT / must not be skipped: a token-identity control baseline -- decode the top-k next-token predictions from the same early hidden state (e.g. via the logit lens / unembedding projection, or plain greedy continuation of just those few tokens), turn that into text, embed it the same way as the real continuations, and test whether the existing semantic probe still beats THIS baseline, not just the mean/random/lexical baselines already tested. This directly addresses the objection that the semantic-recoverability result might be nothing more than a repackaging of already-known token-identity predictability from Future Lens-style methods -- if the semantic probe does not clearly beat this control, say so honestly, that is itself an important and reportable finding. (2) A model-size scaling study using the Pythia suite (pick a reasonable subset of sizes you can fit in the time/GPU/disk budget on GPU 0 only, e.g. something spanning roughly 410m up to a few billion parameters) to see whether semantic recoverability (probe test cosine over baselines) and causal steering effect size grow, shrink, or stay flat with scale. (3) Compare greedy-decoded continuations against sampled continuations (temperature/top-p) for at least the original 1.4b model, to test whether the semantic-recoverability result is an artifact of greedy decoding always producing the single most predictable continuation, or holds up when the actual continuation is less deterministic. Only GPU 0 is available. Produce a report that clearly states, for each of the three priorities, what was found and whether it strengthens, weakens, or leaves unchanged the original hypothesis and its differentiation from Future Lens and ESP.
progress:
Cycle 1 review: ACCEPT - The run appears to have executed the planned protocol successfully and met the stated success_criteria. Specifically: (1) Priority 1 produced the required token-control outputs for pythia-1.4b greedy, including numeric comparisons against the semantic probe and explicit honest reporting that short greedy-rollout controls beat the probe while top-k token-text controls do not. (2) Priority 2 produced scaling_summary.csv for four Pythia sizes including 1.4b and smaller models, with the required fields plus scaling plots. (3) Priority 3 produced decoding_comparison.csv with greedy vs sampled results and reported sampled performance relative to baselines/controls. (4) report.md and final_summary.json were produced and summarize whether each priority strengthens or weakens the original hypothesis. 

There is no indication of an execution mistake that would warrant RETRY. Although one substantive part of the hypothesis was weakened/falsified—because short rollout controls outperform the probe—the experiment was designed to test that possibility and explicitly required honest reporting if controls matched/exceeded the probe. The outputs therefore constitute a successful experiment under the defined criteria, even if the strongest hoped-for substantive outcome was not achieved.
